_about: Held-out evaluation set: 15 fictional UAT reports from week 2 of MedInfo Assist v2.3 UAT Cycle 3, with ground-truth labels. Written and labelled on 4 Nov 2026 by a separate AI agent that was given only the app description, rules, test steps, existing tickets and testers, and was told not to open the AI's instructions or the sample reports. Never shown to the triage AI as examples and not used to tune anything. Used by `npm run eval:holdout`.

reports.text: Checked the HCP details pulled from EML-07 against the signature: title (Prof.), name, institution (Beaumont Hospital) and country all spot on. Much better than last cycle when I was retyping half of it. No issues from me.

Imported EML-11 at 09:31 this morning (that's what the enquiry shows as recieved). Referral form gives the reporting deadline as Tue 3 Nov 14:31. Surely that should be 09:31 tomorrow? It's 5 hours out. If anyone worked to that deadline we'd be referring AEs late.

General feedback from the team lead side: it would save a lot of time if I could tick several enquiries in the inbox and reassign them in one go, e.g. when someone is on annual leave or off sick. At the moment I have to open each enquiry and change the owner one at a time. I did 11 of them this morning to cover a colleague who's off.

MI-20519 is a long one from a hospital pharmacist: four seperate questions, about 2,300 characters. The draft came back in under 10 sec and reads fine, but it only answers Q1 (renal dosing) and Q2 (interaction with ciclosporin). Nothing at all on Q3 (storage outside the fridge) or Q4 (crushing the tablets), and nothing to say anything was left out. I then split it into two enquiries with two questions each and both drafts covered everything. Looks like the end of longer enquiries gets cut off before the draft is written.
Froze on me this afternoon. Had to close it and log back in.

Can't log in. I click 'Sign in with SSO', it goes to the Microsoft page for a second and then back to the sign in page, over and over. Tried 3 or 4 times and cleared my cookies. I'm working from home on my MacBook using Safari, if that matters.

Audit trail for MI-20463. The create, edit and submit-for-review entries all show the correct user, the field changed and a timestamp. However the approval entry (03/11 08:58) shows the user as 'svc-mia-workflow' rather than Dr Whitfield, so the trail does not record which reviewer actually approved the response. We must be able to evidence the approver for every response sent. Repeated on MI-20470 with the same result.

Ireland filter isn't working properly. I'm still seeing UK documents in the results after setting Region = Ireland. We can only send Irish-approved material to Irish HCPs so this needs sorting before go-live.
wrong doc came up again when i clicked on it. not great with an HCP on the phone

Submitted the referral for MI-20494 (imported from EML-11) yesterday. The screen showed SR-30117 and the status changed to 'AE referred' as expected, BUT the referral never arrived in the safety database intake queue on our side. Checked at 11:00 and 14:00 yesterday and again at 08:30 today: nothing. Raised a second one at 08:35 (SR-30121), still not there 15 minutes later. As it stands MI would believe the AE has gone to Safety when it hasn't, and the 24h clock would be missed. Marking as fail even though the MI screen looks right.

The draft for MI-20528 (GP asking about Zentrava for a 12 year old; the SmPC only covers adults) has an extra paragraph at the end saying the product isn't licensed for this use and the information is provided in response to an unsolicited request. It has no citation and isn't in either attached reference, so it fails the 'every statement has a citation' check. It shouldn't be there.

Search for 'renal impairment dosing' worked well. The Corvalix renal SRL was top and the order made sense. One suggestion: could the results show when each document is next due for review/re-approval? The 'Last updated' date doesn't tell you that, and I'd rather not find out after I've cited something that lapses next week.

Added two comments on the draft for MI-20463, one on the renal dose sentence and one on the closing paragraph. Priya then made her edits, and when I opened it again both comments were gone. Not resolved, just vanished. She says she can't see them now either. So I've no record of what I asked her to change.

The top result was the Corvalix clinical overview (around 120 pages). It took roughly 25 seconds to appear in the side viewer; I timed it twice. The 8-page standard response letter below it opened in about a second, so it seems to be only the big files.

Exported MI-20470 (approved yesterday) to Word. The text and the [1] to [3] citations come out fine, but the dose adjustment table by creatinine clearance has lost its structure. Each row is just a line of text with tab gaps and the header row is merged into the first line, so the columns don't line up. The same response exported to PDF looks exactly like the screen, so it's only the Word export. Using Word 365 desktop.
